howItWorks.title: Draft three castaways
howItWorks.text: Pick any three from the cast. Other players can take the same people you did, so do not worry about who is already gone.

howItWorks.title: They score every week
howItWorks.text: Whatever your three earn or lose in an episode is your score for that episode. Points come off the table below and nowhere else.

howItWorks.title: Highest total wins
howItWorks.text: Scores add up across the whole season. Standings update the day after each episode airs.

definitions.Team Immunity Win: Winning immunity as part of a group. Usually your tribe, but it also covers any week the cast is split into smaller teams to compete. Everyone on the winning side gets it.
definitions.Individual Reward Win: Winning a reward challenge for yourself alone. Rewards won as a tribe or team score nothing.
definitions.Win Fire Challenge: Winning the fire-making challenge at final four.
definitions.Immunity Idol Find: Finding a hidden immunity idol yourself. Being handed one does not count.
definitions.Effective REAL Idol: Playing a real idol that saved you from going home. If you would have been voted out without it, it counts.
definitions.Effective FAKE Idol: Playing a fake idol that actually fools the vote.
definitions.Win Advantage: Any non-idol advantage: a journey win, extra vote, vote steal, block a vote, safety without power.
definitions.Shot in the Dark SUCCESS: Playing the Shot in the Dark and drawing safety.
definitions.Make Jury: Awarded once to everyone still in the game the week the jury phase begins.
definitions.Win Survivor: Sole Survivor. The jury vote decides it.
definitions.Quit Game: Walking away from the game on your own.
definitions.Med Visit EVAC: Pulled from the game by medical.
definitions.Voted Out WITH Idol: Going home with an idol still in your pocket.
definitions.Lose Vote: You are at tribal council and cannot cast a vote. Usually a penalty, a vote blocker played on you, or a journey gamble you lost.

rulings.title: Combined challenges count once
rulings.text: When one challenge awards both reward and immunity, it scores as immunity only. You do not get the reward point on top.

rulings.title: Make Jury is a one-time award
rulings.text: Everyone still in the game gets it the week the jury phase starts. Nobody picks it up later.

rulings.title: Every advantage is worth the same
rulings.text: +1 for any non-idol advantage, whatever the show decides to call it that week.

rulings.title: An idol has to work
rulings.text: Playing a real idol only counts if it saved you. If the votes would have sent you home and the idol stopped that, it is +2. If you were never going home that night, playing it is worth nothing.

rulings.title: Rosters are locked
rulings.text: No trades and no replacements, even if one of your three quits or gets pulled by medical.

rulings.title: Late picks
rulings.text: If your three are not in by the deadline, Ryan and Becky decide what happens. There is no automatic rule, so get them in.

rules.tiebreaker: Tied on points at the end of the season? You settle it the way the show does, with a fire making competition between the tied players. If that cannot happen, it goes to whoever's three castaways won the most individual immunity challenges across the season.
rules.scorekeeping: Ryan Bicker and Becky Fitch keep the scoring workbook, and this site is rebuilt straight from it. If a score looks wrong, say something and it gets corrected back to the episode it happened in.

fineprint.Win Advantage: And anything else the show invents. Final call is Ryan and Becky's.

rules.prize: It is $10 to enter. Third place gets their $10 back, second place doubles up to $20, and first place takes the rest of the pot. The exact grand prize depends on how many people play, so we will know the number once all the picks are in.

50.name: Survivor 50
50.subtitle: In the Hands of the Fans
50.blurb: Twenty-four returning players, the largest cast in the show's history, on a season where the fans voted the twists.

49.name: Survivor 49
49.blurb: Kele collapsed early, losing four in a row. The Tres Leches alliance picked up the pieces and ran the table.

48.name: Survivor 48
48.blurb: A chaotic pre-merge, then a quiet two-person alliance that undermined the dominant group from the inside.
